Explore residual associations and groups of facet levels

Source: R/api-residual-network.R
mfrm_residual_network.Rd

After reviewing a fitted measurement model, locate facet levels whose standardized residuals move together across persons. For example, explore criteria that share unexplained variation, or raters with similar residual profiles. This descriptive, signed correlation network complements q3_statistic(), residual PCA and case review.

Usage

mfrm_residual_network(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  facet = "Rater",
  min_pairs = 5L,
  missing = c("pairwise", "complete"),
  min_abs = 0,
  clusters = NULL,
  linkage = c("average", "complete")
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_residual_network'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_residual_network'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

A supported fit_mfrm() result, with ordinary observation-level standardized residuals available from diagnose_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional matching diagnostics; computed once if omitted.

facet

A single fitted facet. Its levels, not persons, are the nodes and the objects clustered. Defaults to "Rater".

min_pairs

Minimum shared persons for a correlation, at least three.

missing

"pairwise" uses the available persons for each pair. "complete" uses only persons with finite aggregated residuals at every selected facet level. No residual is imputed. Clustering requires "complete" so all distances describe the same sample.

min_abs

Absolute correlation threshold for displayed edges, in [0, 1]; default zero retains every nonzero available association. This is a display choice, not a significance threshold. It never changes the correlations or the clustering distance.

clusters

Optional integer number of groups from 2 to the number of levels. NULL skips clustering. The number is supplied, not estimated.

linkage

"average" (default) or "complete" agglomerative linkage.

object

An mfrm_residual_network.

...

Reserved; unused arguments are rejected.

x

An mfrm_residual_network.

Value

An mfrm_residual_network with nodes, all pairs, displayed edges, the correlation matrix, aggregated residuals, cell_counts, person_usage, settings, clustering (status, distance, tree and membership), source model metadata and interpretation notes. plot() returns saved figure data; mfrm_report() and build_summary_table_bundle() connect the result to reporting. Complete RDS archives include person identifiers: review sharing permissions.

Statistical definition

Finite StdResidual values are averaged without weighting within each Person-by-facet-level cell. Pearson correlations across persons define the network. Thus repeated ratings are not treated as independent persons. cell_counts records differing amounts of evidence behind those means. Missing overlap and zero variance produce unavailable (NA) associations, with reasons in pairs; they never become zero edges. All nodes, including isolates, remain in the output. Positive edges indicate co-movement and negative edges counter-movement after the fitted model. These are marginal residual correlations, not conditional/partial correlations or raw Yen Q3.

Unequal assignments, aggregation, estimated Person effects and finite samples can induce residual structure, including negative correlations. Inspect overlap and the rating design before explaining an edge as a substantive relationship. Threshold sensitivity is not a calibrated test. No edge p-values, uncertainty intervals or stability estimates are supplied.

Machine learning and interpretation

Hierarchical agglomerative clustering is unsupervised learning: it merges similar nodes without known outcome labels. With complete-person Pearson correlations, sqrt(2 * (1 - r)) is Euclidean distance between centered, unit-length residual profiles. Average linkage uses the mean between-group distance; complete linkage uses the maximum. Strong negative correlation means dissimilar profiles, not similarity based on absolute correlation. A supplied clusters cuts the resulting stats::hclust() tree with stats::cutree(). Changing min_abs cannot change these groups.

Clustering remains unavailable if any level lacks sufficient common-person variation; the graph and failure reason are still returned. Pairwise deletion can yield an indefinite correlation matrix, so it is not used to manufacture clustering distances. Common-person deletion can select a different population and greatly reduce the sample; inspect person_usage.

Groups are exploratory residual-profile similarities, not latent classes, demonstrated rubric dimensions, rater competence or automatic grounds for excluding a rater. This procedure is not exploratory graph analysis (EGA): Golino and Epskamp (2017) used a graphical-LASSO partial-correlation network and community detection. It is also not a jointly estimated residual-network measurement model. Compare substantive explanations, inspect cases and check sensitivity to sample, linkage and group count. For validation, repeat preprocessing, measurement fitting and clustering within independent or appropriately resampled data; resampling saved residuals alone omits calibration uncertainty. The appropriate resampling unit follows the rating design, including dependencies across persons, tasks and raters.

Where random forests belong

Wesolowski (2019) first used k-means on differential-rater-functioning indices to construct rater types, then random forests to predict those labels. That study motivates a supervised follow-up, not random forests as the clustering algorithm implemented here. Its features and targets differ from these residual correlations. In this supervised use, a forest combines predictions from bootstrap samples and random candidate feature subsets; it requires a declared prediction target and out-of-sample assessment.

A classifier predicting exploratory groups can reproduce the grouping rule without establishing external validity. Fit feature transformations, measurement models and cluster discovery within training data, keep a separate test set and define how new units receive reference labels. Split at the intended generalization unit (for example new raters, persons or tasks); row-wise splitting of repeated ratings can leak information. Out-of-bag error alone does not validate labels constructed on all data. Report class balance, confusion matrices, discrimination/calibration where appropriate and independent substantive outcomes. Feature importance is predictive, not causal. This function does not fit a random forest; use established ML packages for a separately designed prediction study.

References

Wesolowski, B. C. (2019). Predicting operational rater-type classifications using Rasch measurement theory and random forests: A music performance assessment perspective. Journal of Educational Measurement, 56, 610–625. doi:10.1111/jedm.12227 .

Golino, H. F., & Epskamp, S. (2017). Exploratory graph analysis: A new approach for estimating the number of dimensions in psychological research. PLOS ONE, 12, e0174035. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0174035 .

See also

mfrm_cluster_kmeans(), mfrm_cluster_hierarchical(), mfrmr_visual_diagnostics

Examples

ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                 method = "JML", maxit = 300)
net <- mfrm_residual_network(fit, facet = "Criterion", missing = "complete",
                             clusters = 2)
net$pairs                 # association, shared-person count, unavailability
#>     Level1       Level2 ResidualCor  N Reason Displayed
#> 1 Accuracy      Content -0.24351341 48             TRUE
#> 2 Accuracy     Language -0.47046424 48             TRUE
#> 3 Accuracy Organization -0.05276933 48             TRUE
#> 4  Content     Language -0.42513633 48             TRUE
#> 5  Content Organization -0.35361668 48             TRUE
#> 6 Language Organization -0.38506732 48             TRUE
net$clustering$status     # check before interpreting groups
#> [1] "available"
plot(net, type = "matrix", draw = FALSE)
report <- mfrm_report(net)
build_summary_table_bundle(report)$table_index
#>                  Table Rows Cols              Role
#> 1             settings    1   11      study_design
#> 2                nodes    4    4 study_diagnostics
#> 3                pairs    6    6 study_diagnostics
#> 4           clustering    1    2 study_diagnostics
#> 5         source_model    1    3      study_design
#> 6 interpretation_notes    6    1       study_notes
#>                                                            Description
#> 1       Residual definition, sample, threshold and clustering settings
#> 2        All facet levels, displayed degree and exploratory membership
#> 3   All residual pairs, including overlap and unavailable associations
#> 4                  Clustering availability and interpretation boundary
#> 5 Source measurement model; residuals are conditional on its estimates
#> 6          Interpretation boundaries to retain with tables and figures
